title: How the king moves

D0.outcome: Says that the king moves one square in any direction and that it is the piece you must never lose.

D1.outcome: When told 'king', marks the squares a king can step to: free squares and enemy pieces it may safely take; never its own pieces, a square an enemy piece attacks, or a square next to the enemy king.

D2.outcome: In a busy position where the piece is not named, marks every square the king can step to.

D3.outcome: Counts the king moves needed to reach a square and decides whether the king gets there in time, in a position with no hints.

misconceptions: The king can step next to the enemy king.
The king can capture any enemy piece next to it, even a defended one.
The king can move onto a square an enemy piece attacks.
conditions: The king steps one square in any direction onto a free square or an enemy piece.
It may not step onto a square an enemy piece attacks, nor next to the enemy king, and it cannot take a piece that is defended.
contrasts: An enemy piece next to the king may look capturable but be defended, which makes the capture illegal.
A distant enemy piece that attacks none of the squares around the king does not change the king's moves.

soft_prereq_notes.FND.CAPTURE.D1: the 'attacked square' rule is first met inside the king exercises; the full idea of attack follows with captures
